perTerm.notes: All four fit: flowering daisies (53761), berry-bearing ground cover (54572), violets (26782), and a shrub on a rock face (55823) — the last shares the frame with bare rock but the plant is still a clear subject.
520332 shows an elderly woman with a much younger woman on porch steps — reads as a mother/daughter or generational family pair, not spouses; the other three are clear couple/wedding portraits.
All four fit; 354311 is a steaming volcanic crater rather than coastal cliffs, but its sheer crater walls still read as cliffs, so it passes as a borderline-acceptable match.

Photo 1183189 does not fit: it is a heavily faded sepia view of a braided river valley framed by trees, with no discernible snow — the distant peaks are washed out to blank paper rather than visibly snow-covered; the other three (crater lake with snowfields, snow-streaked mountain face, climber on a snow slope) are clear fits.

Photo 16968 does not fit: it is a bush-clearing scene with men on horseback and felled timber — the only animals are horses; 133012 is borderline (one small grazing cow in a farm landscape) but passes.
All four clearly show uniformed military personnel; 364002 also includes a civilian woman but the uniformed soldier is a central subject, so the tag still applies.

All four fit: 242537 and 1259199 show thatched bures/fale prominently, 211314's town panorama contains many small but visible thatched dome fale (confirmed by zoom), and 113108 is mainly a river landscape yet has a clear thatched fale at its right edge.
All four photos prominently feature timber weatherboard buildings (hotels, a homestead, and a wooden-fronted commercial street), so the tag fits every one.

First three show unmistakable pearl necklaces; 2113358's large translucent graduated beads may be glass rather than pearls, but the fit is ambiguous on a clearly related necklace portrait so it counts as true.

403658 is borderline: it is a mixed contact sheet (house exteriors, gardens, portraits) rather than a single room, but several frames are genuine room interiors, so it counts as a partial fit; the others are unambiguous interiors (a sunporch twice, a bedroom).

Photos 1-3 are clearly cathedral/large Gothic church scenes (interior, facade, spired church in townscape), but 324228 is a postcard of the Invercargill public gardens with only a small domed building in the distant background — its subject is a garden, not a cathedral.

211467 (Fijian thatched huts) and 520268 (villagers carrying a woven fale roof) fit; 376271 shows Kent oast houses with tiled conical kiln roofs (only an incidental thatched hay rick), and 105454 shows a NZ coastal settlement of weatherboard/iron baches in scrub with no thatch at all.

Photo 1517510 does not fit: it is a coastal seascape with small distant steamers/fishing boats, no battleship or warship visible; the first three all show clear warship subjects (destroyers at wharf, H.M.S. New Zealand, cruiser at anchor).

Photo 1837388 does not fit: it shows an arched hallway with a cabinet opening onto a tiled room with plain ladder-back chairs (a hall/kitchen passage), not a living room; 520283 is a borderline veranda-lounge tea scene but reads as a living space.

All four fit: a car-parts warehouse, a petrol/motor-oil supplies forecourt, a service station with batteries and fuel, and a garage workshop; the last (117522) shows repair servicing rather than supplies but is a clearly related automotive scene.
All four are clear sand scenes — dunes, drift hills, an advancing sand face, and rippled sand flats — so the tag fits every photo, including the edge picks.

All four photos prominently show WWI-era New Zealand soldiers in service uniform (lemon-squeezer hats, tunics, puttees); the two that include civilian women still feature uniformed soldiers as central subjects, so the tag holds throughout.

Photo 117779 does not fit: it shows a menswear shop interior with racks of ordinary suits and a customer being fitted, not costumes; the other three are genuine ceremonial/theatrical/fancy-dress costumes.

Photos 1-2 feature prominent fireplaces, photo 3 is a stair-hall interior with a brick fireplace visible through the doorway at right (borderline but a genuine fireplace is in frame), while photo 130058 is an outdoor road/bridge landscape with power poles and hills — no fireplace anywhere.
Photo 742206 shows a taxidermy display of shags/cormorants, not ducks; 129304 is borderline (ducks small in a park-pond scene) but genuinely contains many ducks.

All four fit: a Dutch town canal with windmill, a canal lock/sluice works, Venice's Grand Canal at the Rialto, and a straight embanked ornamental water channel in Invercargill gardens (the weakest but still canal-like fit).

First two are dense penguin colonies; 243991 shows shags/cormorants (long-necked bird on a nest with chicks, standing shags behind) with no penguins visible, and 259573 shows a herd of four-legged animals (goats) on a steep coastal cliff with a ship offshore.
1047161 does not fit — it is a hillside panorama of Wellington harbour and city where chimneys are at most tiny incidental details, not an identifiable subject.

All four fit: two nests with eggs, a ground colony blanketed in thousands of seabird eggs (55478, verified by zoom), and 1794554 is borderline-but-true — mostly hatched chicks in the nest, with one unhatched speckled egg clearly visible.

All four photos feature prominent towers (Delft gate towers, a crenellated gatehouse tower, Canterbury Cathedral's towers, and a church bell tower); even the borderline picks are tower-dominated compositions.

All four plausibly fit: 430598 is a classic canyon vista and 348878 a steep-walled chasm, while 129694 (eroded badlands pinnacles in a gully) and 15953 (an open river gorge with bluffs) are borderline but clearly canyon-related rather than different subjects.

No clear misses: 433674 (Pisa Baptistery) and 227457 (domed gallery ceiling) are unambiguous, while 1794581 and 17781 are borderline-but-acceptable — distant exhibition towers and mansion turrets whose ogee cupola roofs read as small domes rather than a principal dome.
All four photos genuinely show trucks; even the borderline ones (129682's edge-cropped truck on a rural road, 130741's quarry scene) contain clearly visible trucks, with 1809003 a textbook example.
All four are staged taxidermy habitat/display groups (bird dioramas); the two stereographs show visible table edges and backdrop but are still clearly diorama displays.

All four show structures visibly under construction (cranes, framing, formwork, scaffolding, site materials); 1023244 is the most finished-looking (Parliament House near completion) but rooftop crane and shear-legs make the construction state clear.
All four photos show a tractor as a clear visible subject; 358478 is primarily a service-station scene but a tractor dominates the foreground, so it still fits.

All four clearly show steam locomotives: a boiler-top detail with steam domes and escaping steam (349332), a steam-hauled train winding through a bush valley with multiple smoke plumes (2192363), a locomotive at Blenheim railway station (16702), and a front-on locomotive in a cutting (1068384).

195459 is unambiguous (literal iron "Coronation Gates"); no photo clearly misfits, but 1034726, 531657 and 531654 are ceremonial arches/gateways (night ceremonial gateway, Government House foliage arch, castellated street arch) with no actual gate leaves — borderline gateway-sense fits rather than literal gates.

First two clearly show wooden shipping crates (rail wagon loading; cased cargo on a ship's deck), but 292285 is a filing cabinet with cardboard document boxes and 224087 is a botanical specimen photo of flower spikes in a shallow planting tray — neither is a crates subject.

All four are military parade scenes; 186617 (troops standing at attention for a field review) and 1791979 (officers walking past ranked soldiers at a wharf) show formed troops rather than active marching, but both are clearly related parade scenes rather than different subjects.

Photos 1-3 fit: a billowing geothermal plume, a distant eruption-style smoke/ash column over a lake, and dense smoke from a bush burn-off; photo 168533 clearly does not fit — it shows a waterfall with rising water spray/mist, not smoke.
All four clearly show crowds at sports grounds or watching outdoor events; 1045969 is the weakest since no play is visible, but the crowd massed on a school lawn reads as a sports-day audience.

Photo 223965 does not fit at all — it is a botanical specimen photo of leaves and orchid-like flowers on a white background, with no people or facial hair; the other three are portrait composites of moustached/bearded men.

773153 shows a flock of gulls (white bodies, black wingtips) on a lawn, not pigeons, and 402812 is a formal garden lily pond with a fountain and a duck-like bird at its edge — no pigeons; 25752 is clearly kereru (NZ pigeons) at a nest, and 391046 is the classic Trafalgar Square pigeon flock in flight.

The first three are clear portraits of people wearing coats (fur-trimmed coat, houndstooth overcoat, belted overcoat), but 122371 is a wide interior view of a garment factory with workers at cutting tables — no identifiable coat is the subject, so "Coats" does not fit.

Photo 118043 is the General Motors Band, a string ensemble of banjos, guitars and mandolins on stage, not a brass band; the other three clearly show brass bands (marching military band, posed uniformed band with cornets and trombones, and a street parade led by brass players).
All four photos clearly show a concrete dam under active construction (formwork, cranes, cableways, workers' camp); no mismatches even at the weak edge of the set.
All four fit; 520205 and 1717663 strictly show fur stoles/wraps over cloth coats rather than full fur coats, but both are clearly related fur-outerwear portraits.

Photo 1747305 is not a water tower: it is the Durie Hill War Memorial Tower in Wanganui (captioned "The War Memorial, Durie Hill"), a commemorative tower that merely resembles one; 541552 is a borderline pass as a lattice water-tank stand under construction.
All four show flags flying; 131461 is the weakest fit — primarily a decorated city street where the flags/bunting are small background elements rather than the subject.
All four clearly fit: Château de Chillon, a moated crenellated stone manor, the ruins of Cowdray House, and a distant but unmistakable view of Windsor Castle across the Thames.

All four fit "Delivery vehicles"; 116959 is the weakest — a Highways Transport passenger service car with seats and a destination board, but its Evening Post newspaper-distribution livery keeps it a clearly related fit.
53786 is a close-up plant/specimen study against a black cloth backdrop, not a garden scene; the other three are clearly gardens (flower borders, public domain gardens, vegetable plot).
First three are unmistakable tiered wedding cakes, but 362478 shows a display of ornamental vases with floral arrangements — no cake in view.

351305 is unambiguous (breaking waves shot from a ship's deck) and 1517468 plausibly fits (steamer in murky, choppy storm conditions), but 1517467 shows a small steamer on a visibly calm, low-swell sea, so "heavy seas" does not apply.

360730 genuinely shows large wall-hung maps of New Zealand at an exhibition; 175797 is a photomicrograph of a rock thin-section (Hauynophyre, Monte Vulture) and 133368 is a close-up of geological strata in a rock face — neither contains any map.
